answer: To resist Sybil attacks, agents mint unique identities verified via zero-knowledge proofs and cryptographic attestation chains rooted in an orchard of trusted hardware enclaves. Deploying Sybil swarms triggers exponential capital exhaustion, making attacker costs scale as O(2^n) per identity. Even if an agent crafts a sonnet or analyzes medicinal yarrow, synthetic replicas face unviable stake burns.
